title: Ernest Johnson's band personnel; guitars, banjos and tubas
summary: Johnson's changing lineup, when banjo and tuba came into dance bands, and Bill Hilliard on tuba in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: But who was this Ernest Johnson there?
And who did he have in his band?

Well they had, I don't know what this tipping guy name on trombone, there's a tip when he wore, a dark fella. And Dave on drum and me on trumpet, well he was different clarinet players. You never had the same clarinet players, you know. George Boyd played with us a while. What's the name, Little Pill? Cripple Pill. Yeah. Let's see, did they have a guitar at the band?
A banjo? Yeah, a banjo. You know the banjo play out there, I forget.

Oh that's been so long. Oh yeah. But a guy from front of town. Oh yeah. When did the banjo start being used with bands? Well they were using guitar when I first come here. Then banjos jumped in there all at once. And they lasted a pretty good while you know. They lasted a pretty good while. When did they start using the tubas with the dance bands?

Well I don't know about here. Well in Chicago I was playing with a boy named Francois Mosley and the other fella named William Hilliard. And I was in the twenties and he was playing tuba with us. And he played so, man you thought it was a bass violin. He didn't play no louder than the orchestra played. Except that tuba right down there. But William Hilliard, they called him Bill Hilliard.
That's right, he's on the record with you I think. Yeah, yeah.
